h1: SEO Audit Services — Find Out Exactly What's Holding Your Website Back
intro: Before you invest in SEO, you need to understand your site's current state — what's working, what's broken, and what's limiting your rankings. GrowZap's SEO audit gives you a clear, prioritized breakdown of every factor affecting your search visibility, with actionable recommendations rather than a data dump you can't act on.

blocks.text: An SEO audit is a comprehensive review of your website's search engine performance across three areas: technical health (how well Google can access and understand your site), on-page optimization (how well individual pages are structured and written), and off-page authority (the quality and quantity of external links pointing to your site). The output is a prioritized list of issues and opportunities — what to fix first, what to improve, and where growth potential exists.

sections.heading: What's Covered in Our SEO Audit

subsections.title: Technical SEO Review
subsections.body: We check site speed, mobile usability, crawlability, indexing status, Core Web Vitals, XML sitemap configuration, and structured data implementation — the infrastructure that determines whether Google can properly access and rank your pages. [Learn more about Technical SEO →]

subsections.title: On-Page SEO Review
subsections.body: We review title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, internal linking, content quality, keyword optimization, and page-level relevance signals across your key pages. [Learn more about On-Page SEO →]

subsections.title: Content Analysis
subsections.body: We identify thin or duplicate content, content gaps relative to competitors, and pages with strong traffic potential that aren't yet optimized for their best-performing queries.

subsections.title: Backlink Profile Review
subsections.body: We assess the quality, relevance, and diversity of your existing backlinks, and flag any potentially toxic links that may be harming rather than helping your authority. [Learn more about Off-Page SEO →]

subsections.title: Competitor Benchmark
subsections.body: We compare your site's visibility, authority, and content coverage against your top competitors to identify where the highest-value opportunities sit relative to your market position.

sections.heading: What You Get After the Audit

blocks.text: Not a 100-page automated report that lists every issue without context — we provide a clear, human-reviewed summary covering:

items.text: Priority issues (fix these first — they're actively limiting performance)
Improvement opportunities (these will meaningfully lift rankings)
A recommended order of implementation based on impact vs. effort

blocks.text: An SEO audit is valuable if you're:

items.text: Starting an SEO campaign and don't know your site's baseline
Experiencing declining rankings without a clear reason
Launching a new website or migrating from an existing one
Wondering whether your current SEO investment is actually being applied correctly
Comparing your site's performance against competitors
We collect access to your Google Search Console, Analytics, and any existing SEO data.
Technical crawl plus manual review of key pages, content, and backlinks.
Your top organic competitors are reviewed alongside your site.
A clear, prioritized document with plain-language explanations of each issue.
We walk you through the audit findings and answer questions before recommending next steps.

items.q: Is the SEO audit really free?
items.a: We offer a free foundational SEO audit covering the most critical technical and on-page issues. Larger sites or audits requiring deeper backlink analysis may involve a fee — we'll confirm scope and any cost during the initial discussion.

items.q: How long does an SEO audit take?
items.a: A standard audit for a small-to-medium website typically takes 5–7 business days, depending on the size and complexity of the site.

items.q: Will the audit tell me exactly why my rankings dropped?
items.a: An audit identifies likely causes for ranking drops — algorithm updates, technical issues, content problems, or lost backlinks — though confirming the exact cause sometimes requires correlating audit findings with the specific timeline of the decline.

items.q: Can I do an SEO audit myself?
items.a: Tools like Google Search Console and Screaming Frog can surface many technical issues, but interpreting what to prioritize, identifying content-level problems, and conducting a proper backlink audit typically requires both expertise and specialized tool access.
